knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes a chi-square test of independence in a contingency table?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Independence uses E_{ij} = (row total × column total)/n in a two-way table. That is not one-sample distributional GOF.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Two-way cross-classification; independence null; E_{ij}=(row total×column total)/n.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating GOF and two-way independence as the same chi-square procedure.

choices.label: A two-way table cross-classifies two criteria. The independence null says the row and column factors do not associate; expected cell counts use the product of marginal totals divided by n.
Independence testing is the same as one-sample goodness-of-fit to a named distribution such as Poisson.
Expected cell counts are always n divided by the number of cells, ignoring the observed margins.
A contingency table classifies only one factor; the second dimension is reserved for expected counts under a continuous Normal model.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Two-way table: rating class × claim/no-claim. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Independence null and expected counts; refuse GOF conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Independence expected counts are products of margins over n. GOF to a named distribution is a different hypothesis and different expected count construction.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Independence null; E_{ij}=(row total×column total)/n; refuse GOF conflation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using GOF-style expected counts, or mangling the margin product formula.

choices.label: H₀: row and column classifications are independent; E_{ij} = (row i total × column j total) / n. This is not the same as a chi-square GOF testing whether one sample follows a named distribution.
H₀: the counts follow a Poisson distribution with mean estimated from the table total; expected counts are that fitted Poisson pmf times n.
H₀: independence; expected counts equal the observed counts in every cell.
H₀: independence; E_{ij} = row i total + column j total, without dividing by n.
